clue.text: Getting on with building somewhere to stay

parts.note: boarding a bus or ship is getting on it
a house is a building

explanation.surface: Someone climbs aboard while a builder works, somewhere a traveller might lodge for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodging house where paying guests take rooms and meals is a place to stay.

clue.text: Exist to chase round girl?

indicators.note: chasing means running behind, so the word for exist comes after the round letter

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
to exist is to live

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to spend their life pursuing a girl around.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is an example: Olive is one girl's name among many.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive is a female first name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: Decide to tackle a crossword a second time?

definitions.meaning: to make up one's mind firmly

definitions.text: tackle a crossword a second time?
definitions.meaning: read as RE- plus SOLVE, to solve a puzzle again

explanation.surface: A solver makes up their mind to have another go at the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a firm decision is to determine something, a direct synonym; the second reading is a playful split into again plus work out.

clue.text: Unlucky Jill has lost Jack

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken out, so a letter goes from the name Jill

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack

explanation.surface: The nursery rhyme pair: Jill has fared badly now that Jack is gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack and Jill went up the hill in the nursery rhyme; here Jack is only the letter J.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill as in ill luck or ill-fated means unfortunate, a sense of bad fortune.

clue.text: Snail, perhaps, having good parts when cooked

indicators.note: cooking mixes and transforms ingredients, so the letters of good and parts are rearranged

explanation.surface: A snail on a plate, with tasty bits once it has been cooked, like French escargots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when cooked' rearranges GOOD and PARTS together; 'having' just joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A snail is one example of a gastropod, the mollusc class including slugs and whelks.

clue.text: A person going after Australian sea air

indicators.note: going after places the person word behind the Australian piece

parts.note: Oz is slang for Australia
one can mean a person, as in one should

explanation.surface: Someone follows an Australian out into the bracing seaside breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is popular slang for fresh, invigorating air at the seaside.

clue.text: Reorganisation of SkyTech Limited

indicators.note: reorganising a company rearranges it, so the letters of the firm's name are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A business news item about restructuring a company called SkyTech Limited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limited' looks like part of the company name (Ltd) but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sketchy knowledge is limited or incomplete, a synonym for scanty.

clue.text: Polluting car stops working with just half of fuel

parts.note: an engine that dies stops working

indicators.note: only half of the word fuel is used, here its back half

explanation.surface: A dirty car breaks down when it has only half a tank.
explanation.definitionFit: Diesel vehicles are known for emitting pollutants such as soot and nitrogen oxides.

clue.text: Scoop small and humble dwelling

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a hovel is a small, squalid dwelling

explanation.surface: A news scoop about a small, modest home.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoop up earth is to dig it with a spade-like tool, a synonym as both noun and verb.

clue.text: Short tum-tum for percussion instrument

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: tum-tum is a childish word for the stomach or belly

explanation.surface: A child calls a small drum a tum-tum.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell is struck to make its sound, so it counts among percussion instruments.

clue.text: General prevalence of money

definitions.meaning: the state of being widely accepted or used, as an idea gaining wide acceptance
the cash in use in a country

explanation.surface: How widespread cash is in general.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea with wide acceptance has wide circulation; the notes and coins of a country are its money.

clue.text: Pack instrument for one with bad designs for bridge?

definitions.text: one with bad designs for bridge?

parts.note: a pack is a deck of playing cards
a harp is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: Someone packs an instrument while scheming against a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge is the card game, not a structure; 'designs' means schemes, not drawings.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheat at card games such as bridge has dishonest designs on the table's winnings.

clue.text: Easy to understand cold king in Shakespeare play

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
Lear is the title king of Shakespeare's King Lear

explanation.surface: A frosty Shakespearean king proves simple to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucid or plain meaning is simple to grasp, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Stately home abroad serving up two teas and ultimate in tiramisu

parts.note: cha is slang for tea, followed by tea itself

indicators.note: the ultimate letter is the final one of the word

explanation.surface: A grand house abroad serves guests tea and tiramisu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving up' only links; nothing is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A French country mansion or castle is a grand house overseas.

clue.text: Political organisation to some extent loses the left

indicators.note: losing a letter means taking it out of the word

parts.note: partly means to some extent
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A political group loses some of its left-wing members.
explanation.definitionFit: A political party is an organised group seeking power, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Incandescent tirade about squandered aid

indicators.note: about means around, so the rant goes around the other letters

parts.note: a rant is an angry tirade

indicators.note: squandered means wasted or scattered, so the letters of aid are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone furious delivers a tirade about wasted aid money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incandescent' suggests rage, but here it means glowing; 'squandered' makes DIA, which 'about' wraps in the tirade.
explanation.definitionFit: Something incandescent glows with light, so it is shining brightly.

clue.text: Ran quickly — grabbing donkey under constant strain

indicators.note: grabbing means holding inside, so one word takes the other in

parts.note: hared means ran fast like a hare
an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: Someone dashes off, catching hold of a donkey while under stress.
explanation.definitionFit: Being harried and stressed by persistent pressure is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Quick-moving US soldier gets in beer

indicators.note: gets in means the soldier goes into the beer

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
GI is the term for an American soldier

explanation.surface: An American soldier nimbly gets into the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimble and able to move fast is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Some comedian backed protest

indicators.note: backed means turned backwards, so the letters run right to left
some of means only part of the word comedian is used

explanation.surface: A comedian supported a protest march.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' looks like support but means reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A demonstration, or demo for short, is a public protest.

clue.text: Run after chap for fruit

indicators.note: after places the run word behind the chap word

parts.note: a chap is a man
to go can mean to run, as a machine goes

explanation.surface: Someone sprints after a man to grab some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The mango is a tropical stone fruit.

clue.text: Part of the eye that's concerning can start to atrophy

parts.note: re means concerning, as in business letters
a tin is a can

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A worrying condition of the eye that can begin to waste away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb but is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The light-sensitive layer at the back of the eyeball is a part of that organ.

clue.text: Intelligent British like wet weather

parts.note: rainy describes wet weather

explanation.surface: Clever Britons enjoy the rain, a joke at the national weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever, having lots of brains, is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Transport is mostly broken

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is used

parts.note: bust means broken

explanation.surface: The transport system is largely out of order.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus is a road vehicle for carrying passengers, a means of travel.

clue.text: Act of putting over excellent situation

parts.note: super means excellent
a position is a situation

explanation.surface: Someone getting a point across lands in a great spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Placing one thing on top of another is the literal sense of laying something over.
